readerContract.humanQuestion: What actually changed in today's two AI-security stories, should I worry, and what should I do?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: A non-sensational explanation of the reasoning-trace replay finding and a clear boundary around OpenAI Daybreak, ending with one proportionate action for each audience.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: No API, cybersecurity or model-development knowledge is assumed.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: Unreadable data is not automatically safely contained; access and context boundaries matter as much as whether a person can read a field.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: The Daily distinguishes an ordinary shared consumer chat from raw developer logs, and distinguishes an everyday ChatGPT model choice from restricted cyber access.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A current two-item Daily briefing that supplies background, mechanism, limits and a useful next move without manufacturing Breaking news.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: Calm, informed and able to explain the difference to someone else.

canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Recheck on paper revision, replication, provider statement, correction, retraction, or any Daybreak access or policy change.

strengthsToUse: State the dated change and scope before interpretation.
Separate evidence, provider framing, inference and unknowns.
Use one bounded analogy and give a specific action.
patternsNotToCopy: Do not copy its Article 50 structure or caller-ID analogy.
Do not inherit any legal claim or publication-status implication.

glossaryAccumulation.producerGuard: Define opaque reasoning block only where it enters the mechanism.
glossaryAccumulation.preventionEvidence: Draft uses connected prose, not a term catalogue.

templateRepetition.producerGuard: Give the two items different structures, headline jobs and closing devices proportionate to their different editorial jobs.
templateRepetition.preventionEvidence: The research finding gets mechanism, action and a line to keep; the access update gets a descriptive headline, organizational check and distinct bottom line.

decorativeAnalogy.producerGuard: Permit one analogy only if its limit is explicit.
decorativeAnalogy.preventionEvidence: Hotel keycard maps unreadable token to over-broad acceptance and stops there.

referenceConfetti.producerGuard: No era reference unless it teaches the mechanism.
referenceConfetti.preventionEvidence: No decorative Rewind Era references appear.

missingMechanism.producerGuard: Trace the block from API response to replay and recovered text.
missingMechanism.preventionEvidence: What actually happened supplies the causal chain.

genericAction.producerGuard: Name the exact affected artifact and remediation.
genericAction.preventionEvidence: Strip opaque fields; revoke or rotate possibly exposed credentials.

jargonBeforeMeaning.producerGuard: Explain the risk before using API-specific terms.
jargonBeforeMeaning.preventionEvidence: The short version and diary boundary precede the mechanism.

disconnectedSystem.producerGuard: Connect provider, API block, compatible model, repository and user action.
disconnectedSystem.preventionEvidence: Each component changes the described attack or mitigation.

joylessInstruction.producerGuard: Use calm direct prose and one memorable line rather than a compliance list.
joylessInstruction.preventionEvidence: Each item ends with a compact line to keep.

purposeTooNarrow.producerGuard: Answer both practical concern and wider system lesson.
purposeTooNarrow.preventionEvidence: Draft covers the incident, its boundary, workplace relevance and non-work reassurance.

mechanismBeforeMotivation.producerGuard: Lead with why the reader should care and what the finding does not mean.
mechanismBeforeMotivation.preventionEvidence: Short version and no-panic boundary precede technical mechanics.

workedExampleOvertakesBookPurpose.producerGuard: Keep examples subordinate to the current-news job.
workedExampleOvertakesBookPurpose.preventionEvidence: Work and home examples are one paragraph and directly transfer the mechanism.

technicalExplainerVoice.producerGuard: Translate API mechanics into ordinary language without losing accuracy.
technicalExplainerVoice.preventionEvidence: Opaque block and hotel-keycard explanation avoid developer shorthand.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: A reported API-boundary flaw exposed hidden content in public raw logs; it is not evidence that every shared chat is exposed. Daybreak is restricted cyber access, not an everyday upgrade.
causalSequence: A provider returns an opaque reasoning block so an application can continue a task.
A block accepted across the wrong context can be replayed to a compatible model.
Recovered text can expose content people believed unreadable, so raw logs require field-level removal and credential remediation.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A workplace team commits a raw coding-agent transcript after checking only visible prompt and answer text.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: A person worries that an ordinary shared-chat link is proven vulnerable by the paper, and learns why the demonstrated scope is different.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Remove opaque reasoning/signature fields from shared raw logs and rotate any credential that may have entered a public session; do not chase restricted Daybreak access for everyday work.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Two-item Daily: answer first, background, mechanism or access boundary, consequence, uncertainty, work/non-work application, source links.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: Do not force both items into identical headings or add service-column filler merely to make the issue look full.

analogyPlan.concept: Encrypted but insufficiently scoped replay token
analogyPlan.analogy: A sealed hotel keycard that opens more rooms than intended
analogyPlan.mapping: The card is unreadable but accepted by a system in an over-broad context, just as an opaque block can be valid yet replayable where it should not work.
analogyPlan.limit: A hotel keycard is not an encrypted AI trace and does not reproduce text; the analogy explains access scope only.
analogyPlan.whyItHelps: It separates human unreadability from safe system containment.

humourPlan.noneReason: The security subject benefits from a calm memorable analogy; jokes would trivialize credential and privacy exposure.

communicationDesign.surfaceAdaptation: The Daily answers first, gives only the mechanism needed to understand the change, states limits beside claims, and ends with a better practical question.

humanQuestion.reason: Readers need to know whether the alarming headline affects them.
humanQuestion.plannedEvidence: Open with what happened and explicitly rule out the unsupported every-shared-chat interpretation.

usefulCuriosity.reason: The surprising part is how encrypted data can still be unsafe.
usefulCuriosity.plannedEvidence: Ask the reader to distinguish unreadable from correctly scoped.

invisibleProcessConcrete.reason: Opaque API replay is invisible to non-developers.
invisibleProcessConcrete.plannedEvidence: Follow the block from one response into a later compatible request.

familiarTechnicalMovement.reason: A bounded familiar model makes access scope visible.
familiarTechnicalMovement.plannedEvidence: Use the sealed hotel-keycard mapping, then return to API context.

limitationsConsequences.reason: A preprint and vendor program both require explicit limits.
limitationsConsequences.plannedEvidence: Name research limits, vendor-framing limits and consumer-chat scope.

humourSurprise.reason: A security exposure does not earn humour in this Daily.

betterNextQuestion.reason: Readers need an action more useful than panic.
betterNextQuestion.plannedEvidence: Ask what raw fields are retained or published and whether the requested cyber access matches an authorized project.

explanationArc.adaptation: Compress the full explanatory arc into a Daily briefing while retaining the causal link and explicit scope boundary.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: Turning a technical preprint into either sensational consumer fear or developer-only sludge.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: Test the exact first item for explain-back of the replay mechanism and transfer to both a workplace raw-log case and an ordinary shared-chat case before integrating the full issue.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: A reader can say what moved, why encryption alone did not contain it, who should act, and who should not panic.
